output.question: Find the top trending Python and Rust repos this week and this month, rank by momentum, and keep only what's relevant to agentic / MCP / dev-tooling with a one-line why-it-matters each.
output.findings:
The current landscape for agentic and dev-tooling is dominated by projects that bridge LLMs with local terminal environments and standardized interfaces. High-momentum Python projects focus on agentic workflows and data preparation, while Rust projects are increasingly used for high-performance agent infrastructure and local system integration.

Top Python momentum includes 'microsoft/markitdown' (universal file-to-markdown conversion for RAG), 'anthropics/claude-code' (agentic terminal coding), and 'chopratejas/headroom' (token-efficient RAG/MCP proxy). These tools are critical for building reliable, context-aware agentic pipelines.

Top Rust momentum includes 'farion1231/cc-switch' (unified assistant for multiple agentic CLIs), 'run-llama/liteparse' (high-performance document parsing for RAG), and 'ogulcancelik/herdr' (agent multiplexer). These reflect a shift toward using Rust for low-latency, resource-efficient agent orchestration and system-level tooling.

Ranking by momentum (stars gained in the observed period), the most impactful projects are: 1. microsoft/markitdown (Python), 2. farion1231/cc-switch (Rust), 3. Alishahryar1/free-claude-code (Python), 4. anthropics/claude-code (Python), and 5. run-llama/liteparse (Rust). Each of these provides essential infrastructure for the next generation of autonomous development agents.
